subject: Marketplace private offer pricing — post-call recap & unit-price mapping
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>
To: Ryan Smith <ryan.smith@aws.amazon.com>, Elena Martinez <elena@brightcart.com>
Cc: Aditya Rao <aditya@redwood.com>, Jonas Weber <jonas@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 15 Jun 2026 09:18:00 -0700
Subject: Marketplace private offer pricing — post-call recap & unit-price mapping

Hi Ryan / Elena,

Thanks again for the call this morning — helpful to align on BrightCart's marketplace path. Quick recap and the asks we discussed: 

- BrightCart is evaluating using Redwood via an AWS Marketplace Private Offer (1-year commit).
- Primary ask: map Redwood unit economics ($/1M tokens) to an AWS private-offer unit price that accounts for AWS marketplace fees and any reseller adjustments.
- BrightCart provided an initial token-volume estimate during the call — please confirm below if anything changes.

Action items we committed to:
1) BrightCart to confirm expected monthly tokens and target budget range (Elena)
2) AWS to confirm marketplace fee % and private-offer mechanics (Ryan)
3) Redwood to produce a unit-price mapping worksheet (attached) showing: Redwood list $/1M -> AWS marketplace price -> BrightCart net $/1M after AWS cuts and any commit discounts.

I attached a pricing worksheet (brightcart_pricing_model.xlsx) with some starter numbers — will iterate once we have the exact marketplace fee and BrightCart's final volume/budget.

High-level note from our side: we typically present a Redwood list price and then map to marketplace price by factoring in the AWS marketplace surcharge. For private offers we can bake in commit discounts so the net price to BrightCart aligns with their target $/1M.

Next call: propose Wed 6/17 11am PT to review the completed worksheet and next steps for the private offer sign flow. Does that work?

Thanks —
Marissa
Marissa Cole

From: Ryan Smith <ryan.smith@aws.amazon.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>, Elena Martinez <elena@brightcart.com>
Cc: Aditya Rao <aditya@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 15 Jun 2026 11:02:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Marketplace private offer pricing — post-call recap & unit-price mapping

Thanks Marissa — great call. A few clarifications from AWS marketplace side: 

- Private offers support a price-per-unit model. The offer can be structured as a committed monthly or annual spend with a custom unit price.
- Marketplace fee / seller reserve: standard 20% uplift is common but varies by partner and program. For private offers we can often adjust the visible price to buyers while handling settlement on the backend.
- We can include a 1-year term commit and apply negotiated discounts on the seller side.

I'll loop in the marketplace PM if we need contract-level exceptions, but for the mapping you requested: assume a 20% marketplace surcharge for modeling and then we'll confirm exact terms once pricing is locked.

Happy to join Wed 6/17 to walk the workflow for issuing the private offer and getting it into the buyer's account.

—Ryan
Ryan Smith
Partner Solutions, AWS Marketplace
ryan.smith@aws.amazon.com

From: Elena Martinez <elena@brightcart.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>, Ryan Smith <ryan.smith@aws.amazon.com>
Cc: procurement@brightcart.com
Date: Tue, 16 Jun 2026 08:25:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Marketplace private offer pricing — post-call recap & unit-price mapping

Marissa, Ryan — thanks for the summary. Confirming the numbers from BrightCart's side: 

- Expected ramp: 15M tokens/month starting Month 1, scaling to 50M tokens/month by month 6 (rough plan).
- Budget: initial target spend approx $4k/month, with flexibility to go to $12k/month if we can prove performance and ROI.
- Target net price: we are looking for a target net cost to BrightCart of ~$250 per 1M tokens (this is the goal after all marketplace fees and any pass-through).

We are amenable to a 1-year commitment in exchange for predictable unit pricing and a commit discount. Please populate the worksheet with an example mapping for 15M and 50M token profiles and show the net BrightCart $/1M after AWS fees.

Elena
Elena Martinez
Head of Procurement, BrightCart
elena@brightcart.com
+1 (415) 555-0198

From: Aditya Rao <aditya@redwood.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>, Jonas Weber <jonas@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 16 Jun 2026 10:30:00 -0700
Subject: Internal: BrightCart mapping (draft numbers)

Marissa / Jonas —

I populated the attached worksheet with a quick draft mapping so we have something concrete to show on Wed:

Assumptions:
- Redwood list price (baseline): $200 per 1M tokens
- AWS marketplace surcharge: 20% -> marketplace-visible price = $240 per 1M
- If BrightCart needs a net of $250/1M, we can offer a commit discount on Redwood list (or absorb via reseller margin) to land there. Example mappings:
  - Option A (commit discount): Redwood list = $215/1M, AWS price = $258/1M, buyer net (after negotiated AWS settlement) ≈ $250/1M (1-year commit, 15M initial).
  - Option B (higher list / reseller margin): Redwood list = $200/1M, AWS price = $240/1M, reseller/partner adds +$10 -> buyer sees $250/1M.

Impact on monthly spend (15M tokens):
- At $250/1M -> BrightCart pay ≈ $3,750/month.
- At $240/1M -> BrightCart pay ≈ $3,600/month.

Notes: we should model both a 15M and 50M profile with stepped commit discounts (e.g., 10% at 15M, 20% at 50M). I'll bring the worksheet to the Wed call and we can present both options (direct commit discount vs. partner/reseller margin).

—Aditya
Aditya Rao
Strategic Accounts, Redwood Inference
aditya@redwood.com

Subject: Re: Marketplace private offer pricing — post-call recap & unit-price mapping

Elena / Ryan —

Thanks for the confirms. Attached is the updated worksheet with the two mapping options Aditya mentioned (brightcart_pricing_model.xlsx) and a private-offer template (aws_private_offer_template.pdf) so BrightCart can see the expected flow. TL;DR of the mappings: 

- Baseline: Redwood list $200 / 1M -> AWS marketplace price (20% surcharge) = $240 / 1M.
- Option A (commit discount): Redwood list = $215/1M -> AWS price ≈ $258/1M -> BrightCart net ≈ $250/1M with a 1-year commit (example).
- Option B (reseller margin): Redwood list = $200/1M -> AWS price $240/1M -> reseller adds ~$10/1M to land buyer net at $250/1M.

For the Wed call I propose we:
1) Pick the preferred mapping approach (commit discount vs. reseller margin).
2) Ryan to initiate the private-offer creation once BrightCart confirms terms.
3) BrightCart to confirm the initial commit level (15M vs 50M profile) so we can finalize discounts.

Next call reminder: Wed 6/17 11:00am PT (I realize the time is in the past relative to this email — if that slot didn't work we can reschedule for Thurs). Please confirm final preferred option and I'll coordinate the private-offer issuance and DocuSign routing.

Thanks everyone — looking forward to getting this live.

Marissa
